newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly panel OKs Indian tribe bond reform.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly panel OKs Indian tribe bond reform.

text.p: A California legislative panel on Wednesday approved a bill clearing the way for Indian tribes to participate in controversial Marks-Roos bond transactions.

The Assembly Committee on Local Government approved Assembly Bill 229 and asked the state's attorney general to review the measure. The final vote count was not immediately available. The bill now advances to the Assembly floor.
The state's so-called Marks-Roos Local Bond Pooling Act allows many types of government agencies to form joint powers authorities to finance capital projects.

Last year, state Treasurer Matt Fong called for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the state's attorney general to investigate several California Marks-Roos bond transactions that involved Indian tribes.

In those deals, the Indian tribes were represented to be the "local agencies" on whose behalf the bonds were issued. But according to the state treasurer, Indian tribes are not eligible to participate in those types of transactions.
Fong said these bond offerings violated the "letter and spirit" of state law, and he urged the SEC and attorney general to investigate the deals.
Assembly Bill 229, by Republican Assemblyman Jim Battin, would amend the Marks-Roos bond act to expand the definition of local agency to include federally recognized Indian tribes.
Battin told the committee Wednesday that his bill would make Indian tribes in California more self-sufficient.
The state Treasurer's office had no immediate comment on the bill's passage.
